title: Blueberry Pancakes
description:
Blueberry Pancakes
Quick. (Check.) Easy. (Check.) Magically nutritious. (Check.) Because Fit
Girls deserve blueberry pancakes too. 350 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Put everything except the last three ingredients into a blender. Blend until totally combined but don't over blend. You want the batter to be thick. Gently stir blueberries into batter.
Heat a non-stick pan on medium. Spray with cooking spray and pour batter in pan to make small silver dollar pancakes. Cook until golden brown on the bottoms then flip. We made two at a time.
Serve with a dollop of syrup and butter and guard your plate from family and roommates and pets.
tips:
TIPS: If you're not a blueberry fan, you can use another fruit in the
pancake batter — or make them plain. Chopped bananas are super
delish. So are strawberries. Mini chocolate chips on special occasions. Add
a tablespoon of chopped nuts for an extra 50 calories. A tablespoon of
granola also adds a nice crunch for around the same extra cals.

Blueberry Pancakes
Quick. (Check.) Easy. (Check.) Magically nutritious. (Check.) Because Fit
Girls deserve blueberry pancakes too. 350 calories. Serves 1.

 INGREDIENTS
 1/3c quick or rolled oats 1/4t cinnamon
 (not instant oats) pinch of salt
 1/3c 2% cottage cheese 1t honey
 1 egg + 1 egg white 1/3c blueberries
 1/4t vanilla 1t syrup
 1/2t baking soda 1/2t butter


 DIRECTIONS
1. Put everything except the last three ingredients into a blender. Blend
 until totally combined but don't over blend. You want the batter to be
 thick. Gently stir blueberries into batter.
2. Heat a non-stick pan on medium. Spray with cooking spray and pour
 batter in pan to make small silver dollar pancakes. Cook until golden
 brown on the bottoms then flip. We made two at a time.
3. Serve with a dollop of syrup and butter and guard your plate from
 family and roommates and pets.
!
TIPS: If you're not a blueberry fan, you can use another fruit in the
pancake batter — or make them plain. Chopped bananas are super
delish. So are strawberries. Mini chocolate chips on special occasions. Add
a tablespoon of chopped nuts for an extra 50 calories. A tablespoon of
granola also adds a nice crunch for around the same extra cals.

title: Brekkie Tostada
description:
Brekkie Tostada
The Brekkie Tostada is pretty and perky and packed with a buncha protein.
(Happy Alliteration Day!) PS: You can sub a wrap and transform this into a
Brekkie Burrito for a few more calories. 340 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Spray a corn tortilla with cooking spray and bake at 350 degrees F for 5-7 minutes to make a hard tostada shell. Or … Busy Girl style, just purchase them pre-made at the store.
Top your tostada shell with two eggs any style (we did scrambled) and then all the other ingredients on the list.
Pick up said tostada and eat it while making a mess of yourself. Or be all proper and fork-and-knife-y.
tips:
TIPS: You can go dairy-free by subbing non-dairy cheese or adding 2T
extra avocado. You can take this out of the egg realm and use sautéed
tofu, chicken, or other meat. This meal is great for lunch and dinner too.
Switch up your cheese, beans, veggies, and salsa to switch up your flavors.
You can even throw a Build-A-Tostada party! (Seriously, throw a Build-A-
Tostada party. Show us the pics.)

title: Apple Pie Baked French Toast
description:
Baked French Toast
Part apple pie, part French toast, all “come over to my house for brunch!”
Each serving with the Greek yogurt is 360 calories. Serves 4.
instructions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Slice bread into cubes and put into the bottom of an 8x8 pan. The bread should fill one full layer with the cubes slightly overlapping.
Whisk eggs with milk and vanilla. Pour on top of the bread cubes. Rotate the bread cubes around so that all sides get covered.

Cut apple into small thin pieces. Toss with lemon juice, a dusting of cinnamon, and sweetener (we used coconut sugar, maple syrup is great too). Add apples to the bread. Lightly toss with your hands so the apples and bread are mixed together.
Bake for 20 minutes or until the egg mixture is cooked through. Serve with 1t maple syrup and 1/2c vanilla Greek yogurt per serving.
tips:
TIPS: You can sub one egg any style as your protein instead of the Greek
yogurt. Cottage cheese also works. This meal reheats very well for a few
days that's why we gave you a bigger recipe. Huzzah!

title: Chia Pudding
description:
Chia Pudding
Chia pudding is one of our all-time favorite foods. We make it with canned
coconut milk to give it a the full out Fit Girl Tapioca pudding-y texture. This
serving is 250 calories. You can also use this as a dessert recipe or snack.
Chia Pudding … #versatile. Serves 1.
instructions: Mix everything together in a mason jar or bowl. Wait 10 minutes. Stir again. You'll notice that it's already becoming pudding-y. Mmmmm. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Top with a pinch of nuts in the morning and enjoy
tips:
TIPS: Canned coconut milk is often in the baking aisle or with the Asian
foods. It's thicker than the coconut milk you get in the boxes. You can sub
regular milk or any alternative milk for this recipe too, just skip the water.
Nothing beats the creaminess of canned coconut milk, though, so give it a
whirl. You can make this a full 350 calories by adding 1/2 cup of fruit and a
tablespoon of nuts. Wait to stir the extras in until the morning when
you're ready to eat it. (PS: We started using vanilla bean paste instead of
vanilla extract. It will change your life forever. Order it online. #worthit.)

title: Hotel Breakfast
description:
Hotel Breakfast
This breakfast is brought to you by childhood memories of the free
“Continental Breakfast” spread at hotels. And also by a love of snack packs.
This is super easy to eat on the go. You can eat it for lunch or dinner too
when you need something tidy and portable. 350 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Arrange your ingredients all pretty like on a plate. Serve with coffee or tea and a hot glass of lemon water. Enjoy while sitting on your real (or imagined) balcony overlooking the ocean.
We used jalapeño yogurt cheese, toasted whole wheat nan, almonds and cashews, low-sodium turkey breast, strawberries, and grapes.
tips:
TIPS: You can get fancy and used smoked salmon here. It's high in sodium
so just watch your portions. If you want to go dairy free, use extra nuts or
meat for the cheese. If you want to go vegetarian, try edamame or
sautéed tofu or tempe sticks seasoned with your favorite spices. Gluten
free is easy, too. Just choose any gluten free bread product that suits your
fancy or add more of the other ingredients. Happy snack packing!

title: Fitnana Split
description:
Fitnana Split
One, because Fitnana is fun to say. Two, because breakfast and dessert love
each other and want to make a baby. Three, because protein. This breakfast
is 250 calories and also works as a snack. Serves 1.
instructions: Slice open your banana. Use a tablespoon to make three “ice cream” scoops out of your cottage cheese.
Top one scoop with diced strawberry, one with melted chocolate, and one with diced pineapple. You have successfully made a Fitnana Split
tips:
TIPS: We're not full at breakfast unless we also have a grain. To make this
a more filling 350 calorie breakfast, serve it on top of 100 calories of
cooked oatmeal (1/3c dry oats) or with a piece of whole grain toast on the
side. You can sub 1/2c vanilla Greek yogurt for cottage cheese if you're not
a cottage cheese fan. To make this dairy-free, use 100 calories of non-dairy
yogurt. (PS: We suggest adding a 100 calorie protein shake on the side if
going non-dairy so you get the same high-protein satisfying breakfast.)

title: Eggs N’ Grits
description:
Eggs N’ Grits
This Fit Girl take on a Southern classic gives you all the comfort with only
250 calories. Huzzah! Serves 1.
instructions: Make grits or polenta according to package directions or try our Lazy Girl shortcut. Put the grits or polenta in a bowl, add 3/4 cup water, microwave for 4 minutes. Stir. Add 2T more water and cook for another minute. (*Cooking times will vary by microwave and brand of grits/polenta.) Stir shredded cheese in after they're done.

While the grits are cooking, sauté onions in a nonstick pan. (A little garlic is also a nice addition.) Make your egg any style in the other half of the pan. We did ours sunny-side up in a heart-shaped egg ring to add a little extra love to our day. When the egg is almost done add the spinach to the onions. It'll cook really quick.
Top the cheesy grits with greens and egg and you're done
tips:
TIPS: To make this a full 350 calorie breakfast, add a second egg and a
piece of turkey bacon. You can sub 70 calories of cooked tube polenta
instead of dry polenta or grits. Prepare it according to package directions
and top with cheese. Vegans can sub an equal amount of non-dairy
cheese and 70 calories sautéed tofu or tempeh for the egg.

LUNCHES

“Are you gonna feed us lunch
already or what?”

title: Classy Lady Salad
description:
Classy Lady Salad
We imagine the commercial for this salad is a girl sitting at a drab cubicle.
And then she takes out her Classy Lady Salad and is instantly sitting at a
chic bistro with super shiny hair. We hope this makes your day feel special.
This salad is 500 calories as pictured because we got carried away with the
nuts and potatoes, but recipe below is for 400 calorie version. Serves 1.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and coat with cooking spray (we used Olive Oil Spray). Peel and cut the beets into teeny cubes. Spray again with cooking spray and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Roast for 10 minutes. Toss around. Cut the sweet potatoes into 1/3 inch half rounds and add to the tray. Spray with cooking spray and roast for another 12 minutes or until done to your liking.

Turn the oven up to 450 degrees F. Pat salmon dry with a paper towel. Place salmon skin-side down on a foil-lined sheet. Brush with olive oil. Bake 4-6 minutes per 1/2 inch thickness. Salmon is done when the color is opaque and salmon flakes easily with a fork. DIRECTIONS CONTD.

Candied walnuts are the secret ingredient here. Put your walnuts in a non-stick pan over medium heat with butter. Once they're nice and golden brown, add the maple syrup and cook for a few seconds longer. Put on a plate to cool.

Lay down your arugula then top with the beets, potatoes, goat cheese, walnuts and salmon. Drizzle with balsamic reduction or, for 30 extra calories, use the dressing listed below. Enjoy your bistro moment QUICK BALSAMIC VINAIGRETTE: Mix 1T balsamic, 1/2t olive oil, 1t honey, 1/4t Dijon & fresh ground pepper to taste. Shake together in a container or blend in a food processor with a clove of roasted garlic. (You can throw the garlic in with the beets when you're roasting them.)
tips:
TIPS: You can use 150 calories of any protein you want for this salad if you
aren't in a salmon mood. Vegetarians can use 120 calories baked tofu
marinated in your favorite dressing or the dressing above (just skip the
honey so it doesn't burn). Fit Girl Vegans and dairy-free girls can sub 50
calories non-dairy cheese for goat cheese or add 2T of avocado. Roasted
carrots are a great sub for beets if you aren't a beet fan. Prepare them the
exact same as the beets in the recipe and use the same amount. You can
use any lettuce you want in place of arugula. Baby mixed greens are great
here, so are spinach, butter lettuce, and romaine. You can even try it with
shredded kale.

title: Veggie Rave Soup
description:
Veggie Rave Soup
Cuz these veggies roll with the wild jalapeño crowd. The recipe is 150
calories a serving and reheats well. Add more broth if needed. Serves 4.
instructions: Put olive oil in the bottom of a soup pot. Add onions, celery, and carrot and sauté until the unions are translucent, a few minutes. Add veggie broth. Moosh the diced tomatoes into smaller pieces with your hands and add them to the pot as well. Add sliced jalapeño rings and chopped cabbage. Cook on medium for 20 minutes.

Add the zucchini, broccoli, and cauliflower. Cook another 10 minutes. Check your veggies. Continue to cook until they reach your desired tenderness. Top with 2T chickpeas per serving. We also topped ours with chives, avocado, and extra hot sauce for only 50 more calories.
tips:
TIPS: To make this into Fit Girl Minestrone, add cooked pasta, a sprinkle of
dried basil and oregano, and fresh parmesan cheese. For Fit-tilla Soup,
serve topped with pre-cooked shredded chicken breast, tortilla chips,
pepper jack cheese, avocado, and a squeeze of lime!

title: Kale Caesar Wrap
description:
Kale Caesar Wrap
Kale and Greek yogurt add a nutrition boost to the eternally popular
chicken caesar wrap. 350 calories, 380 if you add the half cup of raspberries
we put in our picture. Serves 1.
instructions: Boil a pot of water. Put kale into water and boil for 30 seconds. Drain in a colander and rinse with the cold water. Set kale on paper towels to remove excess water.
Blend all the dressing ingredients in a food processor. Toss with the kale, cucumber, and chicken. Heat your wrap in a pan until warmed and top with caesar mix. Wrap and serve
tips:
TIPS: Substitution time! If you're not a kale fan, you can make this the
traditional way using romaine. You can also sub 80 calories of a different
protein for the chicken. You can skip the Greek yogurt and sub 1T light
mayo and thin with a dash of milk. For a vegan dressing, sub 1T light
vegan mayo and vegan parm and thin with a dash of non-dairy milk.

instructions: Slice your mushrooms super thin and sauté them with olive oil cooking spray and a pinch of salt.

Layer with carrots, cucumbers, lettuce, mushrooms, sprouts, banana peppers rounds, and cheese. Top the other slice of bread with avocado and you got yourself a sandwich, son. (Or, rather, daughter.)

title: Magical Unicorn Salad
description:
Magical Unicorn Salad
Hey Sparkle Princesses! Here's some fun from magic land! There's tons of
flexibility with this recipe so long as you follow the rainbow. Because the
unicorns will revolt against you if you don't. 350 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: The name of the game is pick one veggie for every color of the rainbow and prepare them according to your fav prep method. Roast, sauté, steam, or grill. Then pair with 150 calories of your favorite protein.

We roasted the tiny blue potatoes and the bell peppers in the oven at 400 degrees F for 15 minutes on a piece of parchment paper and sprayed them with olive oil and sprinkled them with a pinch of salt.

To make the dressing, cut up the fresh herbs into teeny tiny little pieces then mix everything together. You can adjust the herbs and spices to your personal liking and thin with a little milk if desired. Serve hot or cold. Mix it up or keep the rainbow intact
tips: TIPS: Sub 1T light vegan mayo and a dash of milk to make dairy-free!

title: Curry Noodle Soup
description:
Curry Noodle Soup
Raise your hand if you love curry but are afraid to make it because it looks
crazy hard? [Buncha Fit Girl hands.] We are here to help. This soup is crazy
easy and only requires one pot. 380 calories a serving. Serves 2.
instructions: Cook rice noodles according to package directions. Run under cold water. Divide noodles into two bowls. Rinse out the pot.

Whisk together curry paste, grated ginger (we use a micrograter), with a little of the coconut milk until smooth in the bottom of the pot. Add the rest of the coconut milk and the broth. Bring to a simmer not boil. Add the veggies. (Tip: Add slices of your favorite spicy pepper for a more fiery soup!) Simmer for 5-10 minutes until the veggies are done almost to your liking. Add the tofu and simmer one more minute.
Pour over the noodles. Add chopped basil and an optional squeeze of lime and sriracha. You have made curry soup! You are a goddess
tips:
TIPS: If subbing a meat protein, make sure it's cooked before you add it
into the soup. All kinds of proteins work swell here. #50sSlang

title: Adora-Burger
description:
Adora=Burger
The burgers asked to be called that. They're super friendly and way girlier
than commonly assumed. 350 calories. Serves 1. Carrot Fries are 75 calories
a serving. Serves 4.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Slice carrots into fries and toss with olive oil. Sprinkle with all the seasonings. Bake for 10 minutes. Toss around. Bake for another 5-8 minutes or until done to your liking.

Season your burger with salt and pepper. Put a thumb-print indention in the middle of the burger so it cooks evenly. Heat a frying pan on medium. Spray with cooking spray and fry your burger for 4 minutes on each side or until done to your liking. Top with cheese during the last two minutes of cooking. Pile with remaining toppings and serve
tips:
TIPS: Sub a 200 calorie veggie burger for the beef to make this vegan or
vegetarian friendly. If using 90/10 ground beef, use a 4 oz serving. You can
also sub a chicken breast here to make this an Adora-Sandwich.

title: I’m Going Vegan!
description:
I’m Going Vegan!
About 768 girls we know have been all “I'm going vegan!!!” … and lasted
until they came face-to-face with their next piece of cheese. But this is just
a one meal commitment so the whole “going vegan” thing will prob have a
higher success rate. 400 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Cut the stem off the cauliflower head, stand it upright, and slice into 3/4 inch "steaks." The first pieces will crumble off. You can save those to make Mac & Cheese. (See next recipe!) Dip in a mix of soy sauce, 1/2t of the olive oil, and a sprinkle of dried basil. Flip over multiple times to get thoroughly coated. Bake for 15 minutes at 400 degrees F.

Cut Brussels sprouts in halves and toss with 1/2t olive oil, a pinch of salt, and pepper. When the timer on the cauliflower dings, flip the cauliflower over and add the Brussels sprouts to the baking pan and spray them with olive oil. Bake for 15 minutes. DIRECTIONS CONTD.

Cut polenta into four rounds and sauté in a pan with 1t olive oil on medium for 5 minutes. Leave them alone. No flipping. The, flip them over and add the garbanzo beans, onions, and bell pepper to the other side of the pan and sauté for 5 minutes while the polenta rounds crisp on their other side. Sprinkle the beans and veggies with a pinch of chili powder and cayenne and a (teeny) pinch of salt.

Shake all the tahini dressing ingredients together in a small container until they're wonderfully creamy. Plate your veggies and polenta. Drizzle the tahini over everything. Numnumnumnum. Top with a little fresh ground pepper if desired.
If serving for friends (or showing off on Instagram), put the dressing in a plastic baggie and cut a small hole on the end to get a perfect drizzle. We crown you a vegan — for the next 15 minutes.
tips:
TIPS: You can sub 100 calories of another protein for the garbanzo beans
if you opened your fridge, saw animal protein, and already decided that
you wanted to stop being vegan before cooking dinner. But seriously, buy
the tahini. We know it's expensive and might require a special trip to a
special grocery store, but it's sooooo worth it. It lasts forever (aka a long
time) and also lets you make loads of homemade hummus. (Page 88.) If
you don't like polenta, use 1/3 cup of cooked brown rice, quinoa, or pasta.
Or 3 oz of roasted sweet or regular potatoes.

title: Stupid Easy Mac & Cheese
description:
Stupid Easy Mac & Cheese
This recipe is a) stupid easy, b) full of secret vegetables, and c) almost as
happy-making as getting a hug. 350 calories without topping, 400 calories
with topping. Serves 1.
instructions: Bring a pot of water to boil. Break cauliflower into large florets and add to boiling water. Boil for 8 minutes. Remove cauliflower with a slotted spoon and place on a cutting board. Chop into tiny pieces.

Add pasta to the still-boiling water and cook according to package directions. Drain pasta. Immediately return 3/4c pasta (measure after it's cooked) to the pot and add cheeses. Stir until melted. Add cauliflower and sour cream and stir until well mixed. Use a dash of milk if desired. Serve immediately. (We stirred peas and cayenne pepper into one of ours. Hot sauce or jalapeños are also winners.)

Topping time! Make this while the pasta cooks. Melt the butter in a pan and add the bread crumbs. Sauté until golden brown (it'll happen quick) then sprinkle with a pinch of garlic and onion powder. That's it MICROWAVE VERSION We don't recommend making this recipe in big batches for leftovers, butttt you can do this fun variation which is like having leftovers but way better.
Make a buncha pasta and cauliflower the same way we talked about on the previous page. Store in fridge.
Microwave one serving pasta, cauliflower (3/4c after it's chopped up and cooked), and cheeses for 1 minute. Stir and heat another 30 seconds. Head additional time if needed until cheese is melted.
Immediately add sour cream and stir again. Now you have fresh leftovers
tips:
TIPS: We used gluten-free brown rice & quinoa pasta, which has stolen
our hearts. You can also use any whole wheat pasta — regular is fine if
that's all you have access to at your market. If you don't like cauliflower,
use an equal amount of broccoli and boil for less time. You can
experiment with basically any vegetable in this recipe. Cuz, like, what
veggie doesn't taste ridiculously amazing lathered in cheese and sour
cream?! There's protein in the whole grain pasta and cheese, but if you
want a higher protein meal, only use 1/2c pasta and use those extra 50
calories to stir in 1.5 oz of teeny-tiny diced chicken, a piece of turkey bacon,
or whatever other protein you feel like trying inside. To make this dairy-
free, use equal amounts of vegan cheese, sour cream, and butter.
!
BREAD CRUMBS: Panko is a neat light Japanese bread crumb that's
commonly sold nowadays in the US. Some stores even sell gluten-free
Panko. If you don't have Panko, you can easily make bread crumbs at
home. Bake bread slices on a cookie tray at 325 degrees F for 5-7 minutes
on each side. Let cool. Put in a food-processor and turn it into coarse
crumbs. You have just made homemade bread crumbs. Look out world!

title: Thai Stir Fry
description:
Thai Stir Fry
PEANUT SAUCE! PEANUT SAUCE ON EVERYTHING! BATHE US IN
PEANUT SAUCE! We'll take off the caps lock now. But, seriously, peanut
sauce. We just started making it homemade for the first time and it's like
the world is suddenly in color. Ahhhhhh! 400 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Prepare brown rice according to package directions or be lazy like us and buy it frozen and pop it in the microwave. Measure it cooked.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Peel and devein shrimp. Toss them with lime juice and cayenne pepper. Put them on a pan lined with parchment paper, spray with coconut oil, and roast for 8-10 minutes.
Stir fry the veggies with coconut oil spray. We used pea pods, carrots, broccoli, bean sprouts, and canned baby corn. We pre-steamed the carrots and broccoli so they fried up super quick and evenly.
Blend all the peanut sauce ingredients in a food processor. Toss with the brown rice and veggies. Top with shrimp and serve
tips:
TIPS: You can sub 100 calories of noodles for brown rice and any 150
 calories protein you prefer for the shrimp. This dish works great as
 leftovers. Double the portion and you're set for tomorrow!

title: Porto Pizza
description:
Porto Pizza
You want some pizza for 150 calories? “Shut up.” Ok, but if we shut up we
can't teach you how to make Porto Pizza for 150 calories each. Makes 2.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F. Gently remove the gills from inside the mushroom using a spoon. Spray the tops and bottoms with olive oil spray and put onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Roast for 20 minutes. Remove from oven and pour out the water that has accumulated inside the caps.
Fill each cap with 2T pizza sauce, toppings, and 3T mozzarella cheese. Put back into the oven for 8 minutes or until cheese is melted.

We used olives, green pepper, and artichoke hearts in our front pizza and pre-cooked spinach (to prevent the pizza from getting watery), feta (we used 2T mozzarella and 1T feta), and pickled banana peppers in our back pizza. We sprinkled them with oregano and red pepper flakes because it feels super pizza-shoppy.
tips:
TIPS: You can substitute slices of eggplant for the portobello. Only cook
them for 8 minutes before adding toppings and follow the rest of the
directions as is. Serve these with your favorite protein to make them a
complete meal. Porto Pizzas also make rad afternoon snacks. Just use
vegan cheese to make them dairy-free!

title: Mediterranean Feast
description:
Mediterranean Feast
Three cheers for Mediterranean food! All sexy fresh and fancy yum! We
hope you like this in your tum! (We're delirious.) 400 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F. Cut eggplant into small cubes. Cut garlic cloves in half. Put eggplant and garlic on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and spray with olive oil. Lightly dust with cumin and cayenne. Roast for 15 minutes. Toss. Roast another 10 minutes. Let cool a bit. Mix with cubed feta. Can be served hot or cold.

Prepare the quinoa according to package directions. You can make extra and freeze it for later use. Finely chop the parsley, tomato, cucumber, scallions, and fresh mint (if adding). Mix together with cooled quinoa (measured cooked). Toss with lemon juice, olive oil, and a pinch of salt. Can be served room temperature or chilled. DIRECTIONS CONTD.
Plate your two salads with hummus (you can use store-bought or make your own using our recipe on page 88) and toasted flatbread or pita. Feast away

PS: You can also make your tabbouleh the traditional way with couscous. Just prepare according to the package and use the same amount. You can also also make it with cauliflower “rice.” Just pulse raw cauliflower florets in a food processor until they look like rice. Sub an equal amount. This saves you 50 calories.

title: Fit Girl Parm
description:
Fit Girl Parm
We're having a party called “Embrace Your Inner 8-Year-Old and Chicken
Finger-ize Your Parm.” You're invited. Details below. 400 calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Preheat your oven to 450 degrees F and boil a pot of water. While that's happening, sauté the bread crumbs in a pan sprayed with olive oil until golden brown. It'll happen quickly. Babysit them closely. Set aside on a plate to cool.
Boil your pasta according to package directions. Measure your portion of pasta after it's cooked.

Get your breading assembly line set up. Station One: Mix flour (we used oat flour) with a sprinkle of garlic powder and salt. Station Two: Beat an egg white in a bowl. Station Three: Add the grated parmesan to the cooled Panko and toss together with your hand.

Cut your chicken breast into evenly-sized strips about 1 1/2 inch thick. Roll chicken pieces in flour mixture, dip them in egg mixture and let the excess egg drip off, then roll them in bread crumb mixture, pressing them into the mixture so they get covered in a lot of it. DIRECTIONS CONTD.

Place chicken fingers on a non-stick cookie sheet. Spray with olive oil and bake for 12-14 minutes. Test for doneness.* Your chicken should be white and have no pink inside. Baking time will vary based on thickness of your slices. Add additional time if needed.

While your chicken fingers are cooking, slice your zucchini into “zoodles" using a veggie spiralizer, and sauté in olive oil spray and a dusting of garlic powder and cayenne. You can have as many zoodles as you want. They're super low cal.

Mix the zoodles with the noodles and top with heated jarred marinara sauce. Immediately top with mozzarella cheese and then top with chicken. This will melt the mozzarella. Sprinkle everything with oregano like we did or serve with fresh basil. Or just enjoy as is
tips:
TIPS: To make this vegetarian, turn it into Fit Girl Eggplant Parm! Slice
eggplant into 1/2 inch slices and prepare the same way but cook at 400
degrees F for 15 minutes. Add a sprinkle of dried basil or Italian seasoning
to the bread crumb mixture. (You can do this for the chicken version too!)
Use as many eggplant slices as it takes to use all the bread crumb mixture.
This version is 75 calories less than the chicken parm. (Vegans, use that 75
calories to sub vegan garlic mayo for the egg. Coat both sides of the
eggplant for a non-egg way to get the crumbs to stick.)

!
!
!
 !
 * The US government recommends using a meat thermometer
 to test that chicken is at 165 degrees F.

 SNACKS
“Here, eat my paw while we’re
waiting for our snacks.”

title: PB+B Yogurt Bark
description:
PB+B Yogurt Bark
“Shouldn't this be in the dessert section?” Sure, you can have it for dessert.
But it's also an awesome high protein snack. Snack-ssert! All hail the snack-
ssert! 200 calories a serving. Serves 2.
instructions: Lay a piece of parchment paper down on a jelly roll pan or cookie sheet. Spread out the Greek yogurt with the back of a spoon until it's about 1/2 inch thick. It won't take up the whole sheet.
Slice your banana and place the slices gently down on the yogurt.
Warm peanut butter in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften. Drizzle the peanut butter over the yogurt and banana. Shave chocolate on top using a micrograter.
Freeze overnight then break into chunks to eat! Store unused portion in the freezer in a freezer bag.
tips:
TIPS: You can put all kinds of fruit and nuts down on top of your yogurt
and use any flavor of Greek yogurt you want. Use dairy-free yogurt to
make this vegan. The texture won't be as thick but it will still work. Let the
Yogurt Bark experimentation begin! Can't wait to see your creations!

title: Cute Cukes
description:
Cute Cukes
After fighting with autocorrect over incessantly changing “cukes” to
“dukes,” we have now taught it the word cukes and it will never mess with
us again. And all is well in Fit Girl Land. See below for calories. Serves 1.
instructions: Cut up your cuke to your desired thickness. Have at it with toppings

Here are our toppings from left to right: 1) hummus/artichoke/gluten- free cracker, 2) tomato/sliced cheese stick/dill, 3) avocado/jalapeño/ hot sauce, 4) veggie cream cheese/gluten-free cracker/broccoli.

Here are other some great toppings: salmon, deli meat, shrimp, tuna, turkey bacon, salsa, any kind of cheese, any kind of veggie, any kind of healthy store-bought spread. Think of the cukes as teeny low-calorie sandwich vessels and top away accordingly.
tips:
TIPS: The thing we especially love about Cute Cukes is that you get to eat a
lot of ‘em. A half cucumber has approximately 20 calories aka basically no
calories. To calculate your calories, just add up the calories in your
toppings. Choose 180 calories of toppings to make this a 200 calorie
snack. Choose 80 calories of toppings to make this a 100 calorie snack. You
get the idea. (PS: These also make great party appetizers!)
variations: Choose toppings totaling about 180 calories for a 200-calorie snack, or about 80 calories for a 100-calorie snack. Source examples are listed in the directions.

instructions: Blend everything together in a food processor or sturdy blender.
Pour into popsicle molds.
Freeze overnight.

tips:

foods. Full fat coconut milk is more like a thick cream than an actual milk.

title: Chocolate Shoppe
description:
Chocolate Shoppe
To end this book we wanted to teach you how to make a super-easy box of
truffles as a gift for a friend — or as a gift for yourself! We crown you a Fit
Girl Chocolatier. 60 calories each (not counting toppings). Makes 22.
instructions: Melt chocolate in the microwave for 45 seconds. Stir. Continue to microwave in 20 second intervals and stir until the chocolate is melted. Be careful not to over cook. It's ok if there are tiny bumps.

Immediately stir in the coconut cream and vanilla until fully combined into a gorgeous chocolate frosting mixture. (Super Important Note: You only want the thick coconut cream on top of the coconut milk. Don't shake the can before opening.) Add a sprinkle of cinnamon and pinch of cayenne for a spicy Mexican Chocolate Truffle.

Cover and refrigerate for an hour. Scoop tiny truffles out of the bowl using a teaspoon. Roll them into a ball then roll the truffles into whatever toppings you desire. We used shredded coconut, slivered almonds, graham cracker crumbs, and rainbow sprinkles. These store great in the freezer. (They even taste great right out of the freezer!)
tips:
TIPS: To make truffles the classic way, sub 1/2c heavy whipping cream for
coconut milk. This is called ganache, if you want to get in on the offish
cooking lingo. This version has 10 extra calories per truffle.

title: Brunch for Dinner
description:

Please. Who needs meal “rules.” Eggs like to be eaten whenevs. They told us
this. We speak to eggs. Makes one 380 calorie serving.
instructions: Boil a pot of water, if poaching the egg.

Sauté the onion and sweet potatoes in olive oil until the sweet potatoes are almost done. (We were feeling experimental so used a potato peeler to turn our sweet potato into ribbons, but you can chop it into small cubes too and be normal about it. Especially if you want crispier edges.)

When the water is simmering and looks like champagne, add 1T white vinegar (this helps the egg stay together). Crack the egg into a measuring cup. Gently tip the egg into the simmering water. It will sink. Don't touch it. Leave it alone for 4 minutes. Set a timer.

title: Cherry Pie Fridge Oats
instructions: Refrigerator oatmeal is one of our fav foods and we’re super excited to share it! It’s like having dessert for breakfast. #yesplease Fridge Oats are eaten cold and made the night before. You can make them with any fruit you want. They stay good for up to three days. Our favorite way to make refrigerator oatmeal is in a 12oz or larger jar, but a bowl works just as well. Layer the uncooked oats first then the milk, chia seeds, honey, almond butter, Greek yogurt, and cherries. Stir everything together. A butter knife works great for this if you’re using a jar. (We left it as a parfait just so it looked cute for the picture.) Cover and put in the fridge. Take out in the AM and eat. Ultimate Lazy Girl breakfast. **While we highly recommend plain yogurt, you can use flavored Greek yogurt and skip the honey if you’re not ready to take the plunge. PS: If omitting the chia and almond butter you have 70 extra calories to use during your day.

instructions: Feeling powerful? You will be after you eat this bowl loaded with filling protein, whole grains, veggies, and beans — and it’s great for lunch on the go! To pack ahead, arrange all the ingredients in the container (that’s paprika we put on the hummus and cracked pepper on the chicken) and stir together in any combo you want when lunchtime comes, using the hummus as your dressing. (Just sub 60 calories of another dressing if you don’t dig hummus.) This bowl is great cold or heated, depending on your mood. Keep reading to see how all the ingredients break down. These are some of the staples of Fit Girl friendly eating that we’re gonna come back to throughout the Meal Plan, so we’re taking a few extra moments to explain them a bit! (PS: We found these three- compartment containers through the magic of the internet.) ** Use 1/2c rice instead of 1/3c rice if you don’t like beans. KALE. Kale is one of the super raddest of veggies. It has all sorts of vitamins and minerals that make for healthy bodies and glowing skin. It’s like hyper-spinach. It’s hearty and versatile and comes in a variety of types. (Don’t worry, Spinach. We still love you and will prove it by putting you in some of our recipes too.) How to Steam Kale: Put a steamer basket in a pot, add a couple inches of water, and toss in your kale. (Kale also comes out fine if you don’t have the basket, in our opinion.) You can throw in a finely chopped clove of garlic for extra flavor, which is delish. Cover and let cook about 8 minutes, until the kale is bright green. You can cook less if you want a crunchier kale or more if you want a softer kale. Give it a taste test at 5 minutes and find the kale that you like best. Cooked kale is great hot or cold and an awesome way to add veggies to almost any dish. (PS: We find raw kale a little too prickly for our taste but if you like it raw, feel free to use it that way, too!) BROWN RICE. We use microwavable bags of brown rice when we’re feeling Lazy Girl and make rice in our rice cooker when we’re not. (Although the rice cooker is so easy it’s basically still Lazy Girl.) You can also cook rice on your stove or use boil-in-bag. Just make sure it’s brown (or black) rice, if possible. White is ok if that’s all that’s available to you. You’re welcome to add any spices or herbs to your rice, just no oils. Cilantro and a squeeze of lime makes a great combo, fresh dill is yummy too. Have fun experimenting! Whatever form of rice you choose, follow package directions for prep.

title: Egg McFitFun
instructions: Oh simple brekkie sandwich! How we love thee! Start off by prepping the tomato and avocado and setting out your cheese. Cook the egg over-medium (or however you desire) in a non-stick frying pan using cooking spray. While that’s cooking, toast your English muffin. You can add the tomato to the other side of the pan for a few seconds if you want it heated up. Right after the muffin comes out of the toaster, put the cheese on the bottom half so it starts to melt. You can microwave for 15 seconds if it doesn’t melt enough to your liking. Layer the cheesy side with the tomato, egg, avocado, and a few shakes of hot sauce, if desired. Neat Girl Tip: Mash the avocado before putting it on top of the tomato for a less slidey-aroundy sandwich!

And as you ride around on your cloud, you will high-five people riding around on their clouds. And you will become cloud-riding besties. At least that’s what happened for us. Regardless, polenta is a cinch to make — Lazy Girl like a mother. Put the polenta in a bowl, add 1 & 1/4 cups water, and microwave for 5-7 minutes. Or sauté it in slices then layer with ingredients!

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F.
Place cauliflower into a plastic bag or sealed container with hot sauce; shake to coat.
Mix Greek yogurt and blue cheese in a small container to create your blue cheese dressing for dipping; slice your veggies.

Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil and coat lightly with cooking spray. Place cauliflower on the baking sheet and bake for approximately 8–10 minutes, until tender. Test tenderness by poking with a fork.
These are best enjoyed fresh, so serve right away with your veggies and blue cheese dressing for best results.

title: Greek Chicken Bowls
description: Greek-style chicken bowls with tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, avocado, red onion, Kalamata olives, feta, tzatziki, lemon, and pita.

ingredients.originalText: 1 lb chicken breast (2 boneless, skinless breasts), sliced lengthwise into 4 cutlets
2 cups cherry tomatoes, halved (or chopped heirloom tomatoes)
ingredients.notes: Heirloom tomatoes may be used instead.

ingredients.originalText: 1/2 cup Kalamata olives, pitted and sliced
1 Tbsp extra virgin olive oil, or to taste, divided
Salt and freshly cracked black pepper, to taste
1 cup tzatziki sauce, or more to taste, divided
4 pieces pita bread, cut into wedges
ingredients.notes: For gluten-free bowls, omit pita and use rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice.

instructions: Prepare the tzatziki, then chop and slice the vegetables and toppings.
Coat the chicken cutlets with olive oil, oregano, salt, pepper, and garlic powder. For stronger flavor, refrigerate in the marinade for about 20 minutes and up to 8 hours.
Cook the chicken over medium heat in a grill pan, skillet, or grill for about 4–5 minutes per side, until it reaches 165°F internally. Rest 10–15 minutes, then cut into bite-size pieces.
Divide chicken, tomatoes, cucumber, bell pepper, avocado, red onion, olives, and feta among four bowls.
Finish with olive oil, lemon, salt, pepper, and tzatziki. Serve with pita wedges.
tips: Chicken can also be cooked by air fryer or oven.
Keep tzatziki and pita separate when meal prepping so the bowls stay fresher.
variations: Protein: substitute steak or grilled shrimp.
Gluten-free: omit pita and use white rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice.
Optional additions include chickpeas, radishes, artichoke hearts, carrots, white onion, broccoli, spinach, hummus, scallions, or dill.
substitutions: Pita bread → white rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice for a gluten-free bowl.
glutenFreeNotes: Omit pita bread and use white rice, quinoa, or cauliflower rice. Confirm other packaged ingredients are gluten-free as needed.
mealPrepNotes: Chicken may be marinated up to 8 hours ahead or cooked and refrigerated up to 3 days.
Vegetables can be chopped several hours ahead.
Assembled bowls can be refrigerated for about 1–2 days; store tzatziki and pita separately and add just before serving.
storageNotes: Cooked chicken: refrigerate up to 3 days.
Prepared bowls: refrigerate about 1–2 days with tzatziki and pita stored separately.
